assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy: a cubic-kilometre detector built in Antarctic ice that found a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, then pointed to a first source (the blazar TXS 0506+056) and to Galactic-plane emission. It is an instrument-driven new observational window on cosmic-ray accelerators, which is the kind of discovery I weigh most heavily.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the IceCube concept and programme; Karle was central to AMANDA, the detector construction and the early analyses. Spiering is credited for the wider neutrino-telescope pioneering (Baikal and DUMAND lineage). The prize cap of three makes the AMANDA/Baikal/DUMAND history awkward, and I am not certain who among the many collaboration leaders was decisive for the first evidence.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is well confirmed, including with ANTARES and Baikal-GVD hints, and the source identifications keep strengthening. Recognition is timely and not premature, though the source-population picture is still evolving.
uncertainties: Exact division of credit among Halzen, Karle, Spiering and the DUMAND/Baikal pioneers is unresolved.
Independent confirmation of individual source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) is still at modest significance.
I have not independently verified the detailed collaboration history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson in 2012 completed the Standard Model's particle content and required detectors and analysis of extraordinary complexity. The theory was recognised in 2013, but the experimental discovery has not been, and its lasting importance is beyond doubt.
assessment.attribution: The discovery is the work of thousands in two collaborations. A fair configuration of three would naturally name one or two leaders from each experiment, with the founding spokespersons (Jenni, Virdee, Della Negra) and the spokesperson at announcement (Gianotti) all strong claimants. Any choice of three leaves out a decisive leader and risks looking like an arbitrary pick among collaboration heads.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: both experiments independently confirmed it, and couplings have been measured across Run 2 and Run 3. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: The prize rules and the committee's long-standing reluctance to honour collaboration leaders make the attribution very hard.
Whether Della Negra or Gianotti is the better third choice is a judgement I cannot resolve from the supplied text alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip and hybrid pixel detectors transformed particle tracking and vertexing, are inside ATLAS, CMS and ALICE, and were essential to the Higgs discovery and heavy-flavour physics; pixel descendants also reach medical and X-ray imaging and astroparticle instruments. This is a detector invention with broad and durable impact.
assessment.attribution: Parker is credited for microstrip detectors, and Heijne and Jarron for the hybrid pixel concept at CERN. The split between sensor, readout electronics and bump-bonding means other contributors (for example Kemmer's planar process work, and later pixel chip developers) may also be claimed. The supplied three-person set seems a plausible fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of operation in many independent experiments. Recognition would be late but fits the committee's occasional prizes for instrumentation.
uncertainties: Priority between planar-process silicon sensors, microstrips and pixel hybrids needs checking; I am relying on memory.
The committee has seldom recognised instrumentation alone, so there is a risk it is read as an enabling technology rather than a discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP's full-sky microwave maps fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model to percent precision and gave the first firm measurement of reionization and strong evidence for the geometry and content of the Universe. It is a landmark precision measurement built on careful calibration and systematic control.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was a key instrument and analysis figure and Spergel led theory and parameter extraction. Peebles, Mather and Smoot were recognised separately. The mission was a large team effort, but this trio is a natural, defensible choice.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and confirmed independently by Planck and ground experiments. The prize may be considered partly overtaken by Planck, though WMAP's priority is clear.
uncertainties: The committee may judge that CMB cosmology has been recognised enough (COBE 2006, Peebles 2019).
I have not verified the finer points of the credit split between WMAP and the earlier balloon and ground experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, are the leading platform for redefining the second and enable tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and dark-matter searches. The magic-wavelength idea and its experimental realisation are clean, original and demonstrably consequential.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and Ye drove the performance frontier. Hall and Hänsch were honoured in 2005 for the comb, and Wineland for ion clocks in 2012, so this pair is a clear and compact configuration; Ye also has links to comb work already recognised.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the sense that multiple independent labs reach comparable accuracy, though the redefinition of the second has not yet happened. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes may weigh against it.
Atomic physics is outside my own expertise and I would rely on colleagues for the priority dispute with other lattice-clock groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Event Horizon Telescope delivered the first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A*, a remarkable VLBI technique at 1.3 mm combined with heroic calibration. It opens a new observational regime for strong-field gravity.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging idea and Doeleman led the VLBI instrument and collaboration. Narayan's theoretical modelling of accretion flows matters as well, but the experimental credit is the stronger case. Around 300 collaborators, so the choice of two or three is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably confirmed by multiple epochs and by two sources, but the interpretation (spin, jet launching, polarization) is still developing and the 2020 Nobel already recognised black holes. Somewhat early.
uncertainties: The images are reconstructions that depend on imaging pipelines, so independent confirmation by another array would help.
Whether Narayan should replace one of the two is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2023 pulsar-timing-array evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background is a new window on supermassive black hole binaries and perhaps new physics, obtained through years of precise timing and noise modelling.
assessment.attribution: The result comes from NANOGrav, EPTA/InPTA, PPTA and CPTA. Siemens and McLaughlin lead NANOGrav, while Kramer leads the European effort and the timing methods stem from earlier pioneers (Hellings, Downs, Detweiler, Foster, Backer). Credit is spread across several teams and no single trio seems fair.
assessment.maturity: Premature: the evidence is at about 3 to 4 sigma, the source (binaries versus cosmological) is unsettled, and a clear detection with the expected Hellings-Downs signature is awaited.
uncertainties: Significance has not reached the discovery threshold.
The interpretation of the amplitude is still debated.
Attribution among four PTA collaborations is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: SASE X-ray free-electron lasers gave femtosecond, coherent X-ray pulses and enabled ultrafast structural dynamics and serial crystallography; LCLS, European XFEL and SACLA now operate as major facilities. This is a new instrument class with a wide scientific reach.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini, Kim and the DESY group around Saldin, Schneidmiller and Yurkov all developed the SASE theory and FEL physics. Madey's earlier FEL work and the experimental realisation at TTF/FLASH and LCLS add complications. A three-person set is workable but needs care.
assessment.maturity: Mature: several independent facilities operate, and the science output is large. Timing is reasonable, though the prize might be argued to belong to chemistry or accelerator science.
uncertainties: Priority among Pellegrini, Kim, Saldin and the DESY group, and the role of the facility builders (Galayda, Tanaka, Ayvazyan et al.), is unclear to me.
Whether the committee sees this as physics discovery or enabling technology.
